Hi Alice — great to hear you're ready to go. High-level proposal below; I copied Vivek (implementation lead) and Jordan (runtime engineer) to scope the technical tasks.

Mutual action plan (summary)
- Week 0 (this week): Share SDK quickstart + sample curl and Node/Go snippets. Security signoff checklist: allowlist + header samples + data residency notes.
- Week 1: Sandbox integration with Redwood SDK (dev region). Run synthetic load test, validate token rotation and KV cache behavior.
- Week 2: Staged cutover: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% with rollback plan.

Immediate deliverables (today):
1) SDK quickstart (attached as zip)
2) Migration checklist spreadsheet (attached)
3) Short sample code + recommended timeouts/retries in the email thread below

Rate limit & retry guidance (recommended defaults)
- Client-side per-request timeout: 10s for chat/generation endpoints (adjust to 20s for long sequences).
- Retryable errors: 429, 5xx, network timeouts. Backoff: jittered exponential, base=200ms, cap=5s, max attempts=4.
- For streaming: prefer no retries on partial streams; restart session only when safe.

Security / headers
- Send x-rw-auth: <API_KEY> (rotate with short TTL tokens for SSO).
- Optional: x-rw-project: integralabs-prod to route to dedicated pool.
- We will share IP ranges once you confirm allowlist process.

See attached quickstart and MAP. Vivek / Jordan — can you confirm the staged cutover steps and add any infra caveats?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

> Quick technical notes and a sample snippet for the team.

Thanks — attaching a tiny healthcheck script and the IP ranges below. Healthcheck is a curl that hits /health and validates headers; schedule as cron every 60s during cutover.

Allowlist ranges (prod endpoints):
- 34.210.128.0/20
- 52.15.64.0/19
- 18.198.0.0/16

Healthcheck (bash):
#!/bin/bash
API_KEY="$1"
ENDPOINT="$2"
resp=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "x-rw-auth: $API_KEY" "$ENDPOINT/health")
if [ "$resp" != "200" ]; then
  echo "healthcheck failed: $resp"; exit 2
fi
echo "ok"

I'll post the small script to the shared drive (link below). We should also run a canary test that exercises long-sequence generation (20k tokens aggregated over batches) to validate KV eviction.
